hints: Look carefully at what the colorimeter is tracking. Absorbance starts at zero and rises to a plateau as pyrophosphate substrate is converted to phosphate product.
Think about what more pyrophosphatase does: it gives a faster initial rate but the same starting amount of substrate, so the same final amount of product.
walkthrough:
**Work out what the curve means**

The absorbance rises over time and then levels off. That tells you absorbance is measuring formation of the product, phosphate ions.

When all substrate is used up, no more product can form, so the curve plateaus.

**Apply the effect of more enzyme**

A higher concentration of pyrophosphatase means more active sites available at any moment. So more enzyme-substrate complexes form and product is made faster.

The initial slope (rate) must be steeper for experiment 2, and the plateau must be reached sooner.

**Check the final plateau**

All other variables were standardised, so the initial substrate concentration is the same. The same amount of substrate gives the same final amount of product.

Therefore experiment 2 must level off at the same final absorbance as experiment 1, just faster. That matches graph C.

options.A: Experiment 2 is slower at first and plateaus lower, which would suggest less product. More enzyme cannot reduce the final yield.
options.B: Experiment 2 is faster but plateaus higher. More enzyme speeds up the reaction but cannot create extra product from the same substrate.
options.C: Experiment 2 (dashed) has a steeper initial slope, reaches the plateau sooner, and finishes at the same absorbance. This is exactly the effect of higher enzyme concentration.
options.D: Experiment 2 is slower to reach the same plateau. Higher enzyme concentration should increase, not decrease, the initial rate.
